title: Creating a Design Token Architecture knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Creating a Design Token Architecture”?
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “Primitive tokens” under “Creating a Design Token Architecture”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with creating a design token architecture?
options: Define a small set of named design tokens and reuse them instead of copying arbitrary values.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Define a small set of named design tokens and reuse them instead of copying arbitrary values.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Define a small set of named design tokens and reuse them instead of copying arbitrary values. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “Creating a Design Token Architecture” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
